newsitem.title: CHINA: China income gap widens based on sectors.
newsitem.headline: China income gap widens based on sectors.

text.p: The income gap between those employed in China's highest-paid and lowest-paid sectors has widened in the past five years, a time when economic reform has accelerated, the Economic Daily said on Friday.
The poorest paid made only 70 percent of the income of the richest in 1996, down from 80 percent in 1991, the newspaper quoted State Statistical Bureau figures as showing.
The incomes of employees in the transport and telecommunications sector skyrocketed by 390 percent from 1991 to 1996, the most rapid growth among all sectors, it said.
In the finance and insurance sector, incomes soared by 370 percent in the same period, ranking second, while incomes for those employed in scientific research rose 360 percent, it said.
Employees in geological prospecting had the lowest income increase, or 240 percent in the five-year period, it said.

In 1996, the three highest-paid sectors were finance and insurance, with an average per capita income of 9,448 yuan, scientific research at 8,966 yuan per capita, and transport and telecommunications, where per capita income was 8,778 yuan.

The three sectors in which employees earned the least were geological prospecting, with a per capita average of 6,606 yuan, the commerce and food and beverage sector, where the average was 6,668 yuan, and industry with a per capita average of 6,921 yuan, it said.
